title: Remark
body_md: The choice of $K_s$ must balance computational efficiency and predictive accuracy. On one hand, $K_s$ needs to be relatively large to capture the intrinsic evolutionary behavior and predict future dynamics. On the other hand, an excessively large $K_s$ incurs high computational costs and gradient instabilities associated with a deep computational graph.

title: Remark
body_md:
The motivation for this design is to control the accumulated prediction error over long-time evolution. Unlike short-term learning, $L_{\text{long}}$ starts from the intermediate predicted states $\hat{\bm{U}}_i^{j,l}$, which contain errors accumulated during the preceding $l$ evolution steps. If these states remain close to the corresponding reference states $\bm{U}_i^{j+l}$, they can be regarded as perturbations of the reference trajectory. Minimizing \eqref{eq:L_long} therefore trains the model on states containing accumulated prediction errors and improves the accuracy of the subsequent evolution from such perturbed states, thereby enhancing long-term predictive accuracy.



This interpretation requires a well-pretrained model. Consequently, a sequential training strategy is adopted in the following numerical experiments. Short-term end-to-end learning is first utilized to obtain a pretrained model, followed by long-term end-to-end learning to further reduce accumulated errors.
